Your task is to process the attached commercial insurance application and return the data as a single, valid JSON object.

Data Cleansing: Remove ALL currency symbols (WON, KRW) and commas (,) from from numeric values (e.g., "1,072,950" becomes 1072950.00). 4. Date Formatting: Dates must be returned inDate Formatting: Dates must be returned in 'YYYY-MM-DD' format. 5. Handling Missing Data: If a number is explicitly non-numeric or missing, return the value as 0. 6. Asset Mapping: In Group Insurance, an "Asset" represents an "Insured Group" (e.g., "Group 1 - Executives", "Group 2 - Office Workers"). 7. Section Classification (Adapted for Group Insurance): Section I (Injury): Accidental Death, DisaSection I (Injury): Accidental Death, Disability, Injury Daily Indemnity. Section II (Disease): Disease Death, Diagnosis (Cancer, AMI, Stroke). Section III (Medical): Real Loss Medical Expenses (Silson), Hospitalization. Section IV (Special): Traffic Injury, SpecSection IV (Special): Traffic Injury, Special Activities, etc.
Task: Extract data for the following objects and map them to the JSON structure provided below: 1. InsurancePolicy: Basic policy info (PolicyInsurancePolicy: Basic policy info (Policy No, Dates, Totals, TotalSumInsured). 2. InsurancePolicyParticipant: Parties involved (Co-Insurance company). 3. InsurancePolicyAsset: Map "Insured Groups" here. (e.g., Name: "Group 1", Location: "Head Office Address"). Added HeadCount and JobClass. 4. InsurancePolicyProductClause: Special clauses or warranties mentioned. 5. InsurancePolicyCoverage: High-level coverage groupings linked to each "Asset" (Insured Group). 6. InsurancePolicyCoverageLineitem: Specific benefits under each group (e.g., Injury Death, Cancer Diagnosis, Medical Expense). Rules: Dates: Format as YYYY-MM-DD. Numbers: Remove commas and currency symbols. Links: For "LinkedAssetName" in Coverages, use the exact name of the Group listed in the "assets" array (e.g., "Group 1 - Executives") so the system can link them. Premiums: If the document lists a "Group Total Premium", assign it to SectionPremiumAmount. If it lists individual premiums, sum them up.
